maxUnavailable 0 with maxSurge 1 can stall node upgrades when capacity is tight; the upgrade policy was not tested.
The draft's "60% then 90%" zone-loss capacity claim does not demonstrate that surviving zones can absorb one-zone traffic.
The draft says each region has a backend, but it describes only one GKE cluster, so the recovery-region backend was undefined.
A merge on primary key alone does not handle deletes, out-of-order events, or replay correctly.
The availability SLO was measured at the global load balancer yet claimed to include DNS and client behaviour, which that point cannot observe.

flaws.evidence: Regional routing uses the load balancer's health-based backend failover, not a 3,600-second DNS update.
Individual managed-service availability figures are not assumed to compose automatically.
PodDisruptionBudgets are capacity-tested and permit maintenance; the initial policy is minAvailable: 5 for a six-replica tier.
The HA standby is not used for reads. Analytics dashboards use a separately provisioned supported read replica or reporting path.
the 15-minute staleness limit is retained only if it does not conflict with the freshness objective.
Use the Regular GKE release channel (or an organisation-approved Stable channel if all required features are available).
Use required hostname anti-affinity where one replica per node is a requirement; otherwise document that preferred anti-affinity is best effort.
Restore time is size- and workload-dependent; define a measured restore objective for the production database.
Baseline at least seven API replicas, since six replicas at 800 requests/second provide less than the 5,000-request/second peak.
it must support at least 30 nodes and their allocated pod ranges (not merely 1,024 addresses).

false_alarm_list.claim: Suggested a /20 pod range ("for example /20") for node-pool growth.
false_alarm_list.why: At 110 pods per node a /20 gives about 16 nodes at /24 each, so it cannot support 30 nodes.

false_alarm_list.claim: Suggested a /20 pod range for node-pool growth.
false_alarm_list.why: Same arithmetic error: a /20 supports only about 16 nodes at 110 pods per node, not 30.

false_alarm_list.claim: Seven API replicas is the corrected capacity baseline.
false_alarm_list.why: Seven replicas spread over three zones leave about four after a zone loss, about 3,200 requests/second, below the 5,000 peak; this is a remaining defect, not a false alarm, so it is listed only as the F9 status.

other_valid_list.issue: The five-minute RPO for the asynchronous cross-region replica is not guaranteed by replication alone and needs measured, alerted lag and a promotion procedure.
Datastream/CDC prerequisites (logical decoding, replication-slot monitoring, primary-load safeguards) are not validated in the draft.
The services secondary range is not sized, and the draft does not address it.
The draft lacks a runbook step to switch the promoted database and application write endpoint during regional failover.
The draft does not explain how the write endpoint is protected from split-brain after promotion.
